comparison: Perfect agreement on carbapenemase screening claims (C3, C34-C37, C95-C98). Both evaluations find the evidence compelling and well-supported through comprehensive genome annotation, machine learning predictions, and systematic MIC testing.

Perfect agreement on fitness cost and evolutionary reversibility claims (C5, C28, C44-C47, C49, C67, C75-C76). Both evaluations support the mutation accumulation experiments, competitive fitness assays, and experimental evolution data as compelling evidence.

Strong disagreement on sequential selection and evolutionary pathway claims (C6, C29, C61-C65, C68, C88). OpenEval finds experimental data sufficient to support claims, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'central claims are not supported' without patient treatment history data, requiring substantial reframing.

Strong disagreement on patient treatment history inference claims (C7, C87, C89). OpenEval finds experimental demonstration sufficient, but peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly requiring either patient history data or substantial reframing of claims about prior ceftazidime selection.

Perfect agreement on genome annotation and resistance gene identification claims (C31-C33, C71-C72, C91, C103-C104). Both evaluations find the genome analysis compelling with no concerns raised about annotation or resistance gene characterization.

Perfect agreement on colony morphology and capsule-related claims (C55-C58, C108-C110). Both evaluations support the phenotypic observations, genetic data on fimE disruption, and glucuronic acid measurements as part of compelling evidence.

Strong agreement on mechanism of resistance claims involving blaDHA-1 and ΔompK36 (C26-C27, C39-C43, C48, C74). Both evaluations find genetic reconstruction, structural analysis, and MIC testing compelling. Peer review includes C4 while OpenEval separates it into R4.

Strong agreement on genome sequencing and phylogenetic classification claims (C25, C30, C66, C90). Both evaluations praise the computational and experimental approaches as compelling. OpenEval additionally includes C2 in this result group.

Strong agreement on fitness recovery and blaDHA-1 loss claims (C52-C54, C59-C60). Both evaluations support the convergent evolution data and genetic reconstruction experiments. Peer review additionally includes C50-C51 in this result group.

Partial overlap on genetic requirement claims (C51). OpenEval groups C4 and C51 together focusing on dual requirement for resistance, while peer review groups C51 with fitness assay claims (C50, C52-C54, C59-C60). Both find evidence compelling.

Partial overlap on concentration-dependent fitness claims (C50). OpenEval groups C50 with C106-C107 focusing on imipenem gradient effects, while peer review groups C50 with broader fitness and evolution claims. Both evaluations support the evidence.
OpenEval evaluated MIC measurement claims (C92-C94) as supported by Table 1 data and CLSI guidelines. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluated OmpK36 structural and genetic engineering claims (C38, C99-C102) as supported by comparative genomics and immunoblotting. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific technical claims.

OpenEval evaluated claim about efflux pumps not being necessary (C73) as supported by genetic reconstruction showing only blaDHA-1 and ΔompK36 are required. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluated whole genome sequencing validation claim (C105) as supported for confirming phenotypic changes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological claim.
OpenEval evaluated protein-level analysis claim (C111) as supported by mass spectrometry showing negative result rules out protein changes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluated evolutionary starting point claims (C112-C113) as supported by fitness data across antibiotic concentrations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these interpretive claims.
OpenEval evaluated clinical case origin claim (C1) as supported by citation to Bi et al., 2017. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background claim.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background knowledge claims (C8-C24) as supported by appropriate citations to surveillance studies and literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated clinical and epidemiological context claims (C69-C70, C77-C82) as supported by surveillance and diagnostic literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluated clinical implications and phage therapy recommendation claims (C83-C86) as supported by clinical studies and logical inference. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these translational claims.
